g.text: APPENDIX / GENERATION IS DIFFERENT FROM SELECTION
pass@k is not deployed selection reliability
A benchmark can recognize a passing candidate that an operational selector fails to choose.
At least one of k sampled candidates meets the
specified test; summarize the result over tasks.
State k, task distribution and the test.
Ground-truth recognition can behave like an oracle.
Deployment: can the system choose correctly?
Run the actual verifier, ranker or human-review process.
rejected useful candidates and first-attempt behavior.
Count all candidates, tool calls, verification, review and latency. Compare explicit budgets and acceptance
standards. More attempts can increase success opportunity while also increasing cost and exposure.
Keep partial-credit quality, pass@k, first-attempt success and selected-output reliability distinct. Chen et al.’s
HumanEval paper supplies the metric/selection distinction, not a finance performance result or a general retry policy.
Primary reference: Chen et al., Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (2021); link on page 37 and in notes.
